summary: doctor's auth/env_vars/credentials_location checks must consult the persisted oauth-token.json bundle (via pelotonPersistedBundleStatus in peloton_oauth.go), not only cfg.AuthHeader()/cfg.CredentialSource, which only ever reflect config-file or PELOTON_OAUTH_USERNAME/PASSWORD-derived fields. A user with a valid persisted bundle and no bootstrap env vars set is a real, common, non-error state and must read as configured, not as a failure.
reason: cfg.AuthHeader() is checked on the config loaded before any clientHook runs, so it is always empty for Peloton (the managed auth mints its bearer/session material into a separate on-disk bundle, never into the config's AuthHeaderVal/AccessToken fields at load time). Doctor was reporting "Auth: not configured", "ERROR missing required", and "credentials_location: none" simultaneously with "API: reachable" and successful authenticated calls -- a direct contradiction that cost hours of user time chasing a nonexistent external OAuth provisioning service. Also swept the 'private OAuth wrapper' / 'managed OAuth bundle' wording across auth.go, peloton_oauth.go, doctor.go, helpers.go, agent_context.go, mcp/tools.go, and client.go's peloton-specific hint string -- Peloton has no OAuth wrapper or provisioning service; the CLI just needs PELOTON_OAUTH_USERNAME/PELOTON_OAUTH_PASSWORD set once.
validated_outcome: New tests TestDoctorReportsPersistedTokenWithoutBootstrapEnvVars and TestDoctorReportsNoCredentialsAnywhere drive the real `doctor --json` command end-to-end (real cliutil.SetHomeOverride, a local httptest server for the reachability/credential probes, no live network) and assert the two states are distinguished correctly. Full go build/vet/test suite passes.
